O.outcome_detail: mean number of correct answers on 15-item catheter-use knowledge test among nurses

cells.quote: Subgroup analysis indicates that knowledge scores increased in particular for nurses, staff members without managerial function and staff members frequently placing catheters.
cells.note: The study compared repeated cross-sectional surveys before and after implementation; no control group was included.

O.outcome_detail: mean number of correct answers on 15-item catheter-use knowledge test among staff without managerial function

cells.quote: Subgroup analysis indicates that knowledge scores increased in particular for nurses, staff members without managerial function and staff members frequently placing catheters.
cells.note: The study compared repeated cross-sectional surveys before and after implementation; no control group was included.

O.outcome_detail: mean number of correct answers on 15-item catheter-use knowledge test among frequent catheter users

cells.quote: Subgroup analysis indicates that knowledge scores increased in particular for nurses, staff members without managerial function and staff members frequently placing catheters.
cells.note: Frequent users were defined as healthcare workers placing a catheter a few times a month or more often.

O.outcome_detail: mean number of correct answers on 15-item catheter-use knowledge test among physicians

cells.note: The physician subgroup showed a statistically significant increase; the study compared repeated cross-sectional surveys before and after implementation and had no control group.

O.outcome_detail: 15-item knowledge score on catheter use and complications

cells.quote: The mean number of correctly answered knowledge questions increased significantly between the two survey periods (T0: 10.4, T1: 11.0; p<0.001).
cells.note: Before/after repeated cross-sectional survey with no control group; the intervention bundle included an indication list, daily re-evaluation of catheter need and staff training.

D.treatment: multimodal intervention bundle with indication list, daily review and staff training

O.outcome_detail: 15-item knowledge score on catheter risks, prevention and appropriate indications

cells.quote: For the overall study sample, the mean number of correctly answered knowledge items increased significantly between T0 and T1 (p<0.001) (table 2).
cells.note: Before/after comparison without random assignment or a control group.

D.treatment: multimodal intervention bundle with indication list, daily review and staff training

O.outcome_detail: perception of current practices and organisational culture for safe catheter use

cells.quote: The mean scale score for perception of current practices and culture increased significantly within the overall sample and within all subgroups between the two time points (p<0.001) (table 3).
cells.note: The 13-item perception scale used a 1–7 response scale.

D.treatment: multimodal intervention bundle with indication list, daily review and staff training

O.outcome_detail: attitudes, subjective norms and perceived behavioural control for reducing catheters

cells.quote: The mean score for the scale assessing the determinants of behaviour increased significantly between baseline and follow-up (p<0.001). Positive changes in mean scores were observed for all three constructs (attitudes, subjective norms and perceived behavioural control).
cells.note: The supplied study text states that effect sizes were medium but does not provide a single printed overall effect size.

D.treatment: multimodal intervention bundle with indication list, daily review and staff training

O.outcome_detail: self-reported responsibilities for prescribing, placing, maintaining, removing and reassessing catheters

cells.quote: Self-reported responsibilities concerning IUC management by nurses and physicians changed only slightly over time.
cells.note: Some responsibility items changed significantly, while others did not; no overall effect size was reported.
